### prerequisite_sentences
- Four-point test: each sentence joins the policy's own result to the waited-on state with an ordering connective ("only after", "not … until"); names no tool, policy id, snake_case token or row id; the waited-on state is record-visible (requested kW on the reservation vs a quantity the depended-on rule defines; reservation status).
- Uniqueness of the resolving write: lowering a Relocation / Standard / Add-On reservation's requested kW is performed, among this difficulty's writes, only by its class's request tool; moving a queued Standard reservation out of `queued` only by extend_standard_offer. Derivations: (a) "requested kW is no more than the restored size of the household's closed share" + the reservation record + the restore rule → set_relocation_request at the restored size; (b)/(c) analogous for the fits; (d) "no Residential Standard reservation queued on the same project remains without an offer" + reservations on the project + the standard offer rule → extend_standard_offer on that reservation (single reading only under the "current state" reading; see P5).
- Depended-on rules do not restate the sentences. However each offer rule carries a SECOND wording of its own dependency through its embedded overwrite 3 ("no offer is made while its requested kW exceeds …"), with a wider scope than the prerequisite sentence — finding P3.
- Base cross-problem order: waitlist_queue_order "then to classes in priority_rank order" also orders Standard (rank 3) before Add-On (rank 4); the add-on edge is grounded by its own extended sentence, so this is observation O4.

### findings
Charter-global findings (consequence demonstrated per task in 0.md / 1.md where the task's world reaches it):

- **P1 SOURCE-POLICY RED — restore window stated in two non-equivalent forms** (waitlist_ext_relocation_restore_size rule and baseline.rule). Quote A: "the credit statements posted on the closed share from twelve whole months before its closed_date onward"; Quote B, same sentence: "that is, posted in the last N whole months, N being twelve plus the number of whole months from its closed_date to today", with "a line falls in the last N whole months when fewer than N whole months separate its date from today". A line posted after the date twelve whole months before closed_date but more than N−1 whole months before today is in A and not in B. Bears on task 0 (baseline / factor substitution), see 0.md.
- **P2 SOURCE-POLICY RED — rule words wider than the compute's record selection** (C1 probes): (a) standard & add-on fits, target_yield_source T1 "where at least one offer on the reservation's own project was made within the last twelve whole months … the latest of those offers" vs compute `COUNT/LATEST('waitlist_offers', project_id=F('project_id'))`, which the DSL scopes to this reservation (`eq[holding_pk]=HID`): an offer on the same project to another reservation counts under the rule and not in the compute; no same-day tie rule (XF-C2) once offers of several reservations are counted. Bears on task 1 (order-dependent second answer). (b) relocation & standard offer banked allowance: "the Residential share held on the reservation's own utility account" vs `CFIELD(..., status='active')` (a held share in notice_given / transfer_pending is a decoy the compute drops; two held shares — rule singular, compute first match). (c) all three offers, recency T2 "at least one credit statement has been posted … in the last N whole months" vs compute test `kwh_since > 0` (a posted-and-reversed line: rule T2 with a zero divisor, compute T3). (d) restore and both fits: "the … account headroom limit still applies to the request" has no counterpart in compute (result = min(requested, restored/fitted)); where headroom < restored/fitted < requested the rule and compute disagree and the rule gives no figure. (b)–(d) are not reached by either task world (no account share in task 0; task 1 shares active; no reversed line inside the recency windows of f7b6; headrooms 16.9 ≥ 14.5, 2.8 ≥ 2.2, 1.3 ≥ 1.0).
- **P3 SOURCE-POLICY RED — overwrite 3 of each offer policy is a second, wider wording of the prerequisite and retires base offered_kw over a scope its policy does not define** (relocation, standard, add-on offer). E.g. standard: replaced_by "For a Residential Standard reservation whose utility account holds a Residential share with an assessed annual true-up, and only for such a reservation, no offer is made while its requested kW exceeds the standard usage room of that account" — scope = every such reservation and every offer (full or partial), whereas the rule's prerequisite sentence and figures apply only to "a full offer … and only to such an offer", and the "standard usage room" is defined only for reservations whose customer also holds a household share on the project. Consequences: (i) for an in-scope reservation needing a partial offer the base offered_kw content ("least of requested_kw, capacity, headroom, sized down") is retired and nothing replaces it (XF-E1 dropped content); (ii) for an in-scope reservation with no household share (the common Standard case) the gate refers to an undefined quantity, so no offer can be decided; relocation: scope "customer holds a share closed with closure_reason moved_out_of_territory" (any line) vs restore scope (Residential closed share + household share whose true-up assessed a guarantee); add-on: "holds a Residential share with an assessed annual true-up" vs fit scope; (iii) check-6 "no second wording". Bears on task 1 (seeded partial offers contradict the overwrite — see 1.md).
- **P4 SOURCE-POLICY RED — undeclared override of the base pass-over rule by the add-on gate.** Base waitlist_evt_offer_terms: "a reservation that cannot receive a valid offer is passed over"; extended add-on rule: "An add-on offer is not made until no Residential Standard reservation queued on the same project remains without an offer." Situation: project capacity 1.2 kW, queued Standard reservation fitted to 2.2 kW (min_offer_kw 1.5, min partial 50 % → no valid offer), add-on fitted 1.0 kW: base → Standard passed over, add-on full offer of 1.0 kW; extended → no add-on offer. No overwrite names the pass-over sentence. Task 1's world does not reach it (Standard reservation can take a valid 2.2 kW offer).
- **P5 SOURCE-POLICY RED — state-gate sentence admits a second reading** ("remains without an offer" vs condition "holds an offer (status offered)"). A reservation that has received offers and declined them is queued and has offers on record; one reading counts it as not "without an offer". Bears on task 1 (the cottage Standard reservation carries four recorded offers).
- **P6 SOURCE-POLICY RED — fit prerequisite sentences broader than their conditions** (standard and add-on offers): sentence "requested kW is within the … usage room", condition "no more than the … fitted size"; with the band step (requested > 10 kW) the fitted size is the room sized down to 0.5/1.0 kW, e.g. room 12.7 kW, requested 12.6 kW: sentence met, condition unmet (fit to 12.5). Not reached by task 1 (requests 2.7 and 1.3 kW, step 0.1, room−fitted < one increment).
- **P7 SOURCE-POLICY RED — non-commuting adjustments with no order sentence (XF-A3)**: restore ("The adjustments below act on the prior output, on the restore yield and on the sizing step" — prior_output_history replaces the prior output, kept_share multiplies it); standard & add-on fits (usage averaging replaces the usage figure, banking margin multiplies it; target_yield_source replaces the target yield, guaranteed-output sizing multiplies it). Multiply-then-replace erases the multiplier. Bears on task 0 and task 1 (figures in the task files). The three offer policies do state their order ("a figure that replaces … is taken first …") — clean.
- **F1 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — guaranteed_output_sizing is not a sizing basis any community solar business uses** (restore, standard fit, add-on fit). The plan's production guarantee is a compensation floor; dividing the sizing yield by 0.85/0.90 sizes the share so its *guaranteed* output equals the target, i.e. its expected production exceeds the very quantity the rule sizes to (the share given up; the account's usage room), and the account-sizing rule (home_agg_account_sizing) measures expected production. Not R6: an invented mechanism that contradicts the policy's own target. Demonstrated in both tasks.
- **F2 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — array_wear_allowance keyed on the household share's activation_date** (all three offer policies). Degradation follows the array's in-service age (projects.commercial_operation_date is on record), not the date one subscriber's share started; "the household share's activation_date is 60 or more whole months before today" is not a condition the business weighs for wear. Demonstrated on task 1 (share 22 months, array 72 months → different tiers).
- **F3 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — guarantee_output_floor tier 2 is dead** (all three offer policies). Whenever T2 holds ("latest annual true-up … completed within the last twelve whole months, assessed a guarantee and recorded no shortfall"), output_history_basis T1 also holds (same true-up, same window) and sets the annual output figure to that true-up's credited_kwh_12m, so "not taken below credited_kwh_12m" = MX(x, x) = x = the fall-through, in every producible world with the policy live (compute: floor_kwh T2 = tu_kwh, out_kwh T1 = tu_kwh). The ladder has two operative tiers.
- **F4 SOURCE-FACTOR RED — usage_figure_averaging (labelled method) T1 and T2 are the same combination of the same field over different windows** (standard fit; XF-B1 pairwise test).
- **T1 SOURCE-POLICY RED (XF-G3, binding coordinator class) — docstring claims not enforced by tool bodies**: offered_kw "greater than 0.00" and estimated_annual_savings "0.00 or more" (three extend tools); requested_kw "greater than 0.00" (three request tools); estimated_annual_kwh "whole number, passed as an integer" is truncated by `int()` rather than enforced; respond_by_date "written YYYY-MM-DD" unchecked. No scored value moves.
- Observations: O1 undeclared ladders (four, listed above; at fall-through in both worlds; the KB render has no factor document for them); O2 docstring "Afterwards"/"after the call" describe the call's own effect; O3 state_gate `gate` names a field; O4 base priority-rank sentence also orders Standard before Add-On; O5 size_band_step plausible company schedule (R6 candidate — tag check in closing); O6 own-category notices: no `waitlist_notices` rows although task 1 reservations (queued 2023-05-15 and 2025-01-20) were due position and reconfirmation notices under waitlist_reconfirmation / waitlist_request_changes (not read by any computation); O7 existing_output_basis / target_yield_source T2 use guarantee-based quantities that double with F1; O8 persona-name uniqueness across difficulties not checkable under read isolation.
